newsitem.title: UK: UK faces obstacles in joining EMU in 1999-Labour.
newsitem.headline: UK faces obstacles in joining EMU in 1999-Labour.

text.p: Britain faces "formidable obstacles" in the way of joining a single European currency in January 1999, oppostion Labour party said on Thursday.

But in its manifesto for the May 1 election, it said it would not rule out joining at some stage. "To exclude British membership of EMU forever would be to destroy any influence we have over a preocess which will affect us whether we are in our out," it said. The manifesto reiterated Labour's policy that any decision to join EMU would have to be agreed by the cabinet, then Parliament, and finally the people in a referendum.

Labour, which like the ruling Conservatives officially keeps its options open over European economic and monetary union, used its manifesto to affirm that the success of EMU depends on the genuine convergence of the economies taking part.
Fudging of the Maastricht Treaty rules is unacceptable, it said.

The Labour manifesto also pledged to sign up for the Social Chapter, which guarantees minimum employment rights, but said Labour would retain the national veto over areas such as tax, defence, immigration, budget decisions and treaty changes.
"An empty table at the negotiating table is disastrous for Britain," the manifesto said. "The Social Chapter is a framework under which legislative measures can be agreed."

Britain will take over the European Union presidency in the first half of 1998. A Labour government would push for rapid completion of the single market, enlargement of the EU to include the countries of central and Eastern Europe and Cyprus and reform of the Common Agricultural Policy, the manifesto said.
UK elections are set for May 1 and with Labour riding high in the opinion polls, it would take a massive swing of popular opinion for them not to take power for the first time since 1979.
